pr_title: [CRDB-9007] sql: allow users to view SHOW RANGES with ZONECONFIG privilege
pr_body:
fixes https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/68369

Previously the SHOW RANGES query was limited to users with the admin role.
This was an issue because customers did not want to allow many users access
to the admin role. Therefore, the code has been altered so that users can now either
have access to the admin role or have the ZONECONFIG privilege in order to
view the ranges.

Release note (sql change): allow users who are not admin to SHOW RANGES if ZONECONFIG is granted

User (operator) who is not a member of admin role and doesn't have `ZONECONFIG` privilege:
![Screen Shot 2022-01-26 at 5 53 19 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17861665/151261079-0f933903-f6c2-470d-9842-75200f0f5003.png)
![Screen Shot 2022-01-26 at 5 55 03 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17861665/151261099-ebc92a88-d991-404e-a6d3-d12af6266c70.png)

After granting `ZONECONFIG`:
![Screen Shot 2022-01-26 at 5 55 18 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17861665/151261155-ae14f928-429f-41aa-9e79-8cb3815c2335.png)
![Screen Shot 2022-01-26 at 5 55 40 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17861665/151261179-ec8a25e5-93cd-406d-bacc-528beae3a262.png)
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/75551)

Just posting my thoughts as of now: I'm not sure if it's possible to permission regulate the use of `crdbInternalRangesNoLeasesTable` with the granularity of a privilege like `ZONECONFIG` as privileges are checked on a per descriptor basis. For e.g. if there exists table `A` and table `B` and a new role is created that is not admin and has `ZONECONFIG` privilege on `A`, it is not immediately apparent how within the context of this function we can filter out `B` if the user wants to view ranges on `B`  (through methods other than the sql shell as a new check has been added for this case). It's possible that I don't fully understand how it works seeing as the check added should skip over any tables, database or schema descriptors where there is insufficient permissions yet the query output still can display. Will need to investigate further.
adding Marylia per Nam's suggestion in case she has familiarity/thoughts on the changes

I recently created a new role and the idea was similar to this, so if they had any of two specific roles they had access to things, so I created a new require check for that case that you can take a look [here](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/74715/files#diff-1402bca7aa2ae9e5b623ab3d1e93d918e0f8d652c689c42d644e46611151c9f6R3110-R3137). But that is mostly focus on giving/restricting access on things on DB Console. I don't have enough knowledge on `SHOW RANGES` and `ZONECONFIG` to give an input on how they work (or should work in this case)

Hm, to avoid that, is there a way to update this PR so that if it ends up returning zero rows, it creates the error message at that point? (not sure how easy this is with a virtual table generator, just brainstorming)
I'm gonna merge this towards EoD so if there are any last minute comments, comment now 😄

issue_context.title: The ability to GRANT "SHOW RANGES" for a role
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
We can provide roles with the permission ZONECONFIG, however to debug ranges it is required to be an admin.  As our customer does not want to make all users admin, our customers require the ability to  add `SHOW RANGES` to a role.  

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Create a new role permission that allows users to `SHOW RANGES`

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Giving admin to users, which is not possible in this customers environment. 

**Additional context**

For example, I created a role where we can alter zone config, but can't debug/verify the ranges using `SHOW RANGES`

`operator@:26257/defaultdb> ALTER TABLE defaultdb.test CONFIGURE ZONE USING lease_preferences = '[[+region=local]]',constraints = '{"+region=local": 3, "+region=node3region": 2}', num_replicas=5;
CONFIGURE ZONE 1
operator@:26257/defaultdb> SHOW RANGES from database defaultdb;
ERROR: only users with the admin role are allowed to read crdb_internal.ranges_no_leases
`


gz#9363
comments: @commatter Would it be acceptable if we used the existing `ZONECONFIG` privilege to determine if a user is allowed to run `SHOW RANGES`?

Actually, could you explain a bit more about why `SHOW RANGES` is needed here, and why a non-admin would need it? Why is `SHOW ZONE CONFIGURATION` (https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable/show-zone-configurations.html) not acceptable?

cc @vy-ton @awoods187 for awareness -- this seems like it might be closer to new feature territory.

Hi @rafiss, I will answer both questions.

1. Would it be acceptable if we used the existing ZONECONFIG privilege to determine if a user is allowed to run SHOW RANGES?
A: Yes, I don't see a situation where you would want to administer zone config and not be able to see the results. 

2. Could you explain a bit more about why SHOW RANGES is needed here, and why a non-admin would need it? Why is SHOW ZONE CONFIGURATION (https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable/show-zone-configurations.html) not acceptable?
A:  If users require the ability to determine where data is stored via ZONECONFIG, does it not make sense that they should be able to verify their changes? 'SHOW RANGES' would allow them to do this. Is there an alternative way to verify the location of ranges/leaseholders? Additionally we have a multi-tenant environment where it is not feasible to give every power user admin and there is a hard requirement to not give users admin.
@kevin-v-ngo @thtruo Since you're both looking into range observability, curious if this is something you've considered?

review_comments:
We should make it such that if they have admin OR `ZONECONFIG` they can perform this.

root does not have `ZONECONFIG` on system tables it seems.

```
demo@127.0.0.1:26257/movr> show grants on system.jobs for root;
  database_name | schema_name | table_name | grantee | privilege_type
----------------+-------------+------------+---------+-----------------
  system        | public      | jobs       | root    | DELETE
  system        | public      | jobs       | root    | GRANT
  system        | public      | jobs       | root    | INSERT
  system        | public      | jobs       | root    | SELECT
  system        | public      | jobs       | root    | UPDATE
```
Thanks for the early review Richard! Yes either having the admin role or `ZONECONFIG` makes more sense, changes in progress
@RichardJCai I'm starting to think it may not be possible, see my comment below
